name: capture-page-text-to-field
summary: Park whole-page OCR text into schema fields on initialize, so an LLM/reasoning field (which cannot read the document) has content to work with.

first_page_field.description: schema id receiving the FIRST page's text; plain string field, ui_configuration.type 'data'

last_page_field.description: schema id receiving the LAST page's text; on a 1-page document it receives the same text as first_page_field

max_chars.description: per-field truncation cap; keeps a long page from bloating the annotation and the downstream prompt

provenance: Lifted from a field-built function hook (2026-07) and verified live: the page_data semantics re-probed against a purpose-built 25-page document (20-page default, silent >20 truncation, ascending result order, texts-has-no-position), and the downstream contract confirmed on an org with reasoning fields enabled — a hook-written context field is picked up by the reasoning field on the same run.
notes: Reasoning fields are feature-gated and separately billed, and the gate is NOT enforced by the schema API — a non-enabled org accepts the config and simply never produces a value. A reasoning field is a normal datapoint (type string) marked by ui_configuration.type 'reasoning'; sending type 'reasoning' is rejected. Verified: a reasoning field DOES recalculate from a field this hook writes in the same event chain, so one pass is enough. Fails OPEN: any fetch/parse error logs and writes empty strings rather than blocking the document. Uses granularity=texts so no line joining or reading-order reconstruction is needed. Requires sideload: ["schemas"] on the hook (TxScript) — clearing it fails every run before any useful work. Prefer two narrow labelled fields over one concatenated blob, since context entries are presented to the model by field label.
